$comment: THE FOUR SEASONS - canonical prompt slot order. Every character prompt MUST be assembled by joining the slots below in the declared order with ', '. Do not reorder, do not omit a slot, do not inline extra clauses. The wiki outfit sheets carry the assembled string; this file is the source of truth for how it was built.

slot_definitions.subject: Age, nationality, social role, height and build. Never omit - a prompt without a subject generates a different person on every run.
slot_definitions.eyes: Shape, eyelid, iris colour, brow. Chapter-invariant.
slot_definitions.top: Upper garment: material, colour, and how it is worn.
slot_definitions.bottom: Lower garment: length, silhouette. For one-piece outfits, describe the skirt portion here.
slot_definitions.legwear_shoes: Hosiery plus footwear. The lace-vs-velcro distinction is load-bearing for characterisation - keep the fastening explicit.
slot_definitions.tone: Seasonal palette, contrast level, skin and lighting. Derived from the character's personal-colour assignment.
slot_definitions.expression: The 6-stage expression fragment. Replaces nothing - it is inserted between eyes and framing. See expression_stages.
slot_definitions.framing: Shot framing for expression sheets. Fixed across all characters so the six panels are comparable.

forbidden: real person names (the face_model frontmatter field is an internal casting note, never a prompt token)
pixel art / 16-bit / retro game style tokens (concept dropped)
chapter-specific breakdown state (put that in a per-scene override, not the base prompt)
stage-1 illustration as the IP-Adapter reference for a stage-2 realistic render (style would follow the reference back to illustration)

negative_prompt: worst quality, low quality, bad anatomy, bad hands, missing limbs, extra limbs, cropped, text, watermark, signature, jpeg artifacts, blurry

tachibana-hiiragi.stage2_constraint: REQUIRED. Hiiragi is 19 but deliberately designed to read younger (childlike face, soft rounded build, regression to childhood as her theme). Under a photorealistic style that design can produce output reading as a minor. Stage 2 for this character must hold unambiguously adult facial structure and proportions, and any output that does not must be discarded rather than adjusted. Her youthfulness is carried by styling and behaviour, never by making the body or face look like a child's.

expression_framing: bust-up portrait, head and shoulders, facing viewer, plain neutral background, even soft lighting

pipeline.$comment: Two stages. Illustration is not a rejected style - it is the specification layer where human and model agree on what is decided. Realistic is the deliverable.

stage1_illustration.purpose: Fix and agree the features. Exaggerate the readable signs (sweat beads, circular blush, light leaving the eyes) so both a human and a model can confirm what is settled.
stage1_illustration.tone_suffix: clean anime illustration, character design sheet style, flat colours, clear linework, plain background
stage1_illustration.published_as: 仕様画像（wikiに「仕様」として掲載）

stage2_realistic.tone_suffix: photorealistic, natural skin texture and pores, soft directional lighting, shallow depth of field
stage2_realistic.structure_from: Stage 1 output, via canny_map or depth_map into ControlNet. This is what carries the agreed expression and pose across the style change.
stage2_realistic.identity_from: A realistic reference of the same character. IP-Adapter inherits style from its reference, so the stage-2 reference must already be realistic - a stage-1 illustration would drag the output back to illustration.
